findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, truncated read)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed, recoverable error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use .map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) on read_to_string

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string is imperative shell I/O fused into the function that constructs domain records
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic is entangled with file I/O, making the function untestable in isolation and violating functional core / imperative shell
findings.fix: split into a shell function that performs file I/O and calls a pure parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> calculation

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is logging (I/O) inside the record-construction closure
findings.failure_mode: side effects in the pure-data path mean the function cannot be reasoned about deterministically; logs leak into any consumer that calls this function
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from the parsing path; if instrumentation is needed, return a count or log in the shell layer after parse completes

findings.problem: parts[0] indexes the split result without checking length; a line without a comma has exactly 1 element
findings.failure_mode: malformed input line panics at runtime via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::Invalid(line.to_string())) to get name and value parts safely

findings.problem: parts[1] indexes the split result without checking length; a line with a trailing comma or only one field has no element at index 1
findings.failure_mode: malformed input panics at runtime via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once and destructure into (name_str, value_str) so missing fields produce an error rather than an index panic

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value, overflow, or empty string
findings.failure_mode: any non-numeric sensor value in the file causes a process crash instead of returning a typed parse error

findings.problem: (..) as u16 is a lossy cast; values in range 0x10000..=0xFFFFFFFF truncate silently
findings.failure_mode: sensor values > 65535 silently wrap, producing incorrect domain data with no error signal
findings.fix: u32::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| Error::ValueOutOfBounds(value_str.to_string())) or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.problem: load_sensors has no domain cap on the number of records; untrusted file length drives unbounded Vec allocation
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfiguration can supply a huge file causing OOM or denial of service
findings.fix: count lines or validate file size first, apply a domain cap, then use Vec::try_reserve(validated_cap).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation) before the parse loop

findings.problem: load_sensors fuses file I/O (line 9), logging I/O (line 16), parsing, and domain construction into one function
findings.failure_mode: the entire data pipeline is untestable as a pure unit; every call depends on filesystem state and produces console side effects
findings.fix: extract a pure fn parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and have load_sensors read the file, strip the logging, and call parse_records

findings.problem: name: String is a raw primitive with no constraints; any string including empty or whitespace is valid domain state
findings.failure_mode: illegal sensor names (empty, whitespace-only, non-UTF8 edge cases) can exist in the domain, breaking invariants downstream
findings.fix: newtype-wrap with struct SensorName(String) and a smart constructor that rejects empty/whitespace-only names, returning a typed error

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for all parts when only the first two are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and memory copy for every line; wastes memory and CPU on intermediate vectors
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...) to get (&str, &str) directly without any Vec allocation

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() clones a String from the Vec when split_once gives a &str that can be owned via .to_owned() or the name newtype constructor
findings.failure_mode: redundant heap allocation per record with no correctness benefit
findings.fix: after split_once, pass name_str.to_owned() (or name_str.into()) to the SensorName constructor

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this I/O-bound function; no baseline or regression threshold is defined
findings.failure_mode: performance cannot be measured or tracked; any optimization claim is unverified
findings.fix: add a Criterion or custom benchmark measuring file read + parse throughput, establish a baseline, and set a regression threshold

findings.problem: no [dev-dependencies] or [[bench]] section; no benchmark crate configured in Cargo.toml
findings.failure_mode: cannot run cargo bench or any performance verification commands
findings.fix: add criterion or a similar benchmarking crate to dev-dependencies and define a [[bench]] target

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied parse-throughput claim
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf) for hot-path identification
no allocation evidence (allocations-per-call, heap footprint) for the Vec::collect pattern
no second-ring evidence (assembly listing) to verify bounds-check removal or vectorization after fixes
no command evidence that cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test pass
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands executed. The function load_sensors contains 7 absolute-law violations (unwrap x2, hidden I/O x2, unchecked indexing x2, lossy cast) that are unfixable without source changes. Even after repair, missing benchmarks and absent clippy/fmt gates leave performance and hygiene unverifiable. The architecture requires splitting into shell (I/O) and calculation (parsing) layers, replacing raw String with SensorName newtype, and adding try_reserve with a domain cap.
